**The argument — TTW reference notes**

Makinen's case is talent accumulation: over two springs the Texas staff signed the No. 1 and No. 3 ranked recruit and transfer classes per 247Sports, which to him makes this probably the most talented locker room in the country. He allows the talent still has to be developed but credits Steve Sarkisian with having done exactly that, taking Texas to the playoff title game two years ago. He reads last season's expectations as unrealistic, with the pressure on the programme and on Arch Manning visible every week, and points out the Longhorns still won 10 games despite a 5-7-1 ATS record.

*Rests on:* recruiting and portal classes; coaching (Sarkisian); quarterback (Manning)

**The argument — TTW reference notes**

Makinen expects one Group of Five team in the playoff this year rather than the two that got in last season, and names Boise State as the likeliest candidate as they move to the new Pac-12. Running his updated power ratings against the 2026 schedule produced a +1.7 win difference he calls one of the biggest he has ever had. He argues the oddsmakers are crediting the new conference's strength too generously when Boise State is its clear favourite, notes Maddux Madsen returns at quarterback as a senior and Spencer Danielson is in his fourth year, and identifies the opener at Oregon as the only likely loss on the slate.

*Rests on:* power rating versus schedule; quarterback (Madsen); coaching (Danielson, year four); conference realignment
